feature_details.Rage:
You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren't wearing Heavy Armor. You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
  While active: **Damage Resistance** — Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. **Rage Damage** — bonus damage on Strength-based weapon/Unarmed Strike hits, per the Rage Damage column. **Strength Advantage** — Advantage on Strength checks and saving throws. **No Concentration or Spells** — can't maintain Concentration or cast spells. **Duration** — lasts until the end of your next turn, ends early if you don Heavy Armor or are Incapacitated; extend it each round by making an attack roll against an enemy, forcing an enemy to save, or taking a Bonus Action to extend it. Maintainable up to 10 minutes total.
feature_details.Unarmored Defense: While not wearing armor, base AC = 10 + Dexterity + Constitution modifiers. A Shield doesn't break this benefit.
feature_details.Weapon Mastery: Use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice (e.g. Greataxes and Handaxes). Change one choice whenever you finish a Long Rest. Gain more kinds at higher levels per the Weapon Mastery column.

feature_details.Danger Sense: Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless Incapacitated.
feature_details.Reckless Attack: On your first attack roll of the turn, you can attack recklessly: Advantage on Strength-based attack rolls until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time.

feature_details.Barbarian Subclass: Choose Path of the Berserker, Path of the Wild Heart, Path of the World Tree, or Path of the Zealot. You gain each subclass feature at your Barbarian level or lower.
feature_details.Primal Knowledge: Gain proficiency in another skill from the level-1 Barbarian skill list. While raging, you can make an ability check using Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival as a Strength check instead of its normal ability.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Extra Attack: Attack twice instead of once when you take the Attack action.
feature_details.Fast Movement: Speed +10 ft while not wearing Heavy Armor.

feature_details.Instinctive Pounce: As part of the Bonus Action to enter Rage, you can move up to half your Speed.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Brutal Strike: If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo Advantage on one Strength-based attack roll (that roll mustn't have Disadvantage). If it hits, the target takes an extra 1d10 damage of the weapon/Unarmed Strike's type, and you cause one Brutal Strike effect of your choice: **Forceful Blow** — target pushed 15 ft away, you can then move up to half Speed toward it without Opportunity Attacks; **Hamstring Blow** — target's Speed -15 ft until start of your next turn (only the most recent Hamstring Blow applies).

feature_details.Relentless Rage: If you drop to 0 HP while raging and don't die outright, make a DC 10 Constitution save; success sets your HP to twice your Barbarian level instead. DC +5 each subsequent use, resets to 10 on a Short or Long Rest.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Improved Brutal Strike: Adds two more Brutal Strike effects: **Staggering Blow** — target has Disadvantage on its next save and can't make Opportunity Attacks until start of your next turn; **Sundering Blow** — before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll by another creature against the target gets a +5 bonus (only one Sundering Blow bonus at a time).

feature_details.Persistent Rage: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Rage uses (once per Long Rest). Your Rage now lasts 10 minutes automatically without needing to extend it each round; ends early only on Unconscious (not just Incapacitated) or donning Heavy Armor.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Improved Brutal Strike: Brutal Strike's extra damage increases to 2d10, and you can apply two different Brutal Strike effects at once.

feature_details.Indomitable Might: If your Strength check or save total is less than your Strength score, use that score instead.

feature_details.Epic Boon: Gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat you qualify for; Boon of Irresistible Offense recommended.

feature_details.Primal Champion: Strength and Constitution scores each increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

feature_details.Bardic Inspiration:
You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is repre- sented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which is a d6.
  Using Bardic Inspiration. As a Bonus Action, you can inspire another creature within 60 feet of your- self who can see or hear you. That creature gains
one of your Bardic Inspiration dice. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.
  Once within the next hour when the creature fails a D20 Test, the creature can roll the Bardic Inspira- tion die and add the number rolled to the d20, po- tentially turning the failure into a success. A Bardic Inspiration die is expended when it's rolled.
  Number of Uses. You can confer a Bardic Inspira- tion die a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all ex- pended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
  At Higher Levels. Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain Bard levels, as shown in the Bardic Die column of the Bard Fea- tures table. The die becomes a d8 at level 5, a d10 at level 10, and a d12 at level 15.
feature_details.Spellcasting:
You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Bard spells, which appear in the Bard spell list later in the class's description.
  Cantrips. You know two cantrips of your choice from the Bard spell list. Dancing Lights and Vicious Mockery are recommended.
  Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list.
  When you reach Bard levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Bard spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Bard Features table.
  Spell Slots. The Bard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you fin- ish a Long Rest.
  Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Bard spell list. Charm Person, Color Spray, Dissonant Whispers, and Healing Word are recommended.
  The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Bard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Bard spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
For example, if you're a level 3 Bard, your list of
prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.
  If another Bard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Bard spells for you.
  Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Bard spell for which you have spell slots.
  Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcast- ing ability for your Bard spells.
  Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Musical Instru- ment as a Spellcasting Focus for your Bard spells.

feature_details.Expertise:
You gain Expertise (see "Rules Glossary") in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Performance and Persuasion are recommended if you have profi- ciency in them.
  At Bard level 9, you gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.
feature_details.Jack of All Trades:
You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn't otherwise use your Proficiency Bonus.
  For example, if you make a Strength (Athletics) check and lack Athletics proficiency, you can add half your Proficiency Bonus to the check.

feature_details.Bard Subclass: You gain a Bard subclass of your choice — College of Dance, College of Glamour, College of Lore, or College of Valor. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Bard levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Bard level or lower.

feature_details.Font of Inspiration: You now also regain all expended Bardic Inspiration uses on a Short Rest (not just Long Rest). You can also expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration.

feature_details.Words of Creation: You always have Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill prepared. When you cast either, you can target a second creature within 10 ft of the first target.

feature_details.Spellcasting: Cantrips — know 3 of your choice from the Cleric list (Guidance, Sacred Flame, Thaumaturgy recommended); replace one on each level-up; learn another at levels 4 and 10. Prepared Spells — start with 4 level-1 spells (Bless, Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt, Shield of Faith recommended); the list grows per the table; can be freely re-chosen on a Long Rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability; a Holy Symbol works as a Spellcasting Focus.
feature_details.Divine Order: Choose one sacred role — **Protector** (proficiency with Martial weapons, training with Heavy armor) or **Thaumaturge** (one extra Cleric cantrip; bonus equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum +1, to Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks).

feature_details.Channel Divinity:
Two uses (regain one on a Short Rest, all on a Long Rest; more at higher levels per the table). If an effect needs a save, DC = your spell save DC. Effects known at level 2:
  - **Divine Spark**: as a Magic action, target a creature within 30 ft — roll 1d8 + Wisdom modifier, and either restore that many HP to it or force a Constitution save (fail: Necrotic or Radiant damage, your choice, equal to the total; success: half, rounded down). Extra d8 at Cleric levels 7 (2d8), 13 (3d8), 18 (4d8).
  - **Turn Undead**: as a Magic action, each Undead of your choice within 30 ft makes a Wisdom save; on a failure, Frightened + Incapacitated for 1 minute (tries to flee you each turn); ends early on damage, your own Incapacitated condition, or your death.

feature_details.Cleric Subclass: Choose Life, Light, Trickery, or War Domain. You gain each subclass feature at your Cleric level or lower.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Sear Undead: Whenever you use Turn Undead, roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1d8); each Undead that fails its save takes Radiant damage equal to the total (doesn't end the turn effect).

feature_details.Blessed Strikes: Choose one (if you'd get either option twice from an older-book subclass, only apply it once): **Divine Strike** — once per turn on a weapon attack hit, extra 1d8 Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice); **Potent Spellcasting** — add your Wisdom modifier to damage dealt by Cleric cantrips.

feature_details.Divine Intervention: As a Magic action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a Reaction; cast it without a spell slot or Material components. Once per Long Rest.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Improved Blessed Strikes: Whichever Blessed Strikes option you chose improves — **Divine Strike** extra damage becomes 2d8; **Potent Spellcasting** lets you grant Temp HP equal to twice your Wisdom modifier to yourself or a creature within 60 ft when a Cleric cantrip deals damage.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Greater Divine Intervention: When using Divine Intervention, you may choose Wish as the spell; doing so means you can't use Divine Intervention again until you finish 2d4 Long Rests.

feature_details.Druidic:
You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. While learning this ancient tongue, you also unlocked the magic of communicating with animals; you always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared.
  You can use Druidic to leave hidden messages. You and others who know Druidic automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check but can't decipher it without magic.
feature_details.Primal Order:
You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.
  Magician. You know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to nature gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1).
  Warden. Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.
feature_details.Spellcasting:
You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Druid spells, which appear on the Druid spell list later in the class's description.
  Cantrips. You know two cantrips of your choice from the Druid spell list. Druidcraft and Produce Flame are recommended.
  Whenever you gain a Druid level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list.
  When you reach Druid levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Druid Features table.
  Spell Slots. The Druid Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.
  Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Druid spell list. Animal Friendship, Cure Wounds, Faerie Fire, and Thunderwave are recommended.
  The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Druid levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Druid Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Druid spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Druid, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.
  If another Druid feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Druid spells for you.
  Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells with other Druid spells for which you have spell slots.
  Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Druid spells.
  Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Druid spells.

feature_details.Wild Companion:
You can summon a nature spirit that assumes an animal form to aid you. As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape to cast the Find Familiar spell without Material components.
  When you cast the spell in this way, the familiar is Fey and disappears when you finish a Long Rest.
feature_details.Wild Shape:
The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a Bonus Action, you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned for this feature (see "Known Forms" below). You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a Bonus Action.
  Number of Uses. You can use Wild Shape twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
  You gain additional uses when you reach certain Druid levels, as shown in the Wild Shape column of the Druid Features table.
  Known Forms. You know four Beast forms for this feature, chosen from among Beast stat blocks that have a maximum Challenge Rating of 1/4 and that lack a Fly Speed (see "Animals" in "Monsters" for stat block options). The Rat, Riding Horse, Spider, and Wolf are recommended. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your known forms with another eligible form.
  When you reach certain Druid levels, your number of known forms and the maximum Challenge Rating for those forms increases, as shown in the Beast Shapes table. In addition, starting at level 8, you can adopt a form that has a Fly Speed.
  When choosing known forms, you may look in other sources for eligible Beasts if the Game Master permits you to do so.

  Rules While Shape-Shifted. While in a form, you retain your personality, memories, and ability to speak, and the following rules apply:
Temporary Hit Points. When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Druid level.
Game Statistics. Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block, but you retain your creature type; Hit Points; Hit Point Dice; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies and use your Proficiency Bonus for them, in addition to gaining the proficiencies of the creature. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast's stat block is higher than yours, use the one in the stat block.
No Spellcasting. You can't cast spells, but shapeshifting doesn't break your Concentration or otherwise interfere with a spell you've already cast.
Objects. Your ability to handle objects is determined by the form's limbs rather than your own. In addition, you choose whether your equipment falls in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the GM decides whether it's practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment based on the creature's size and shape. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with the form. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect while you're in that form.

proficiencies: Martial Weapons with the Light property

feature_details.Martial Arts: Mastery of Unarmed Strikes and "Monk Weapons" (Simple Melee weapons; Martial Melee weapons with the Light property). While unarmed or wielding only Monk Weapons, unarmored, and shieldless: **Bonus Unarmed Strike** — make an Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action. **Martial Arts Die** — roll it in place of normal Unarmed Strike/Monk Weapon damage (die size grows per the table). **Dexterous Attacks** — use Dexterity instead of Strength for attack/damage rolls (and Grapple/Shove save DC) with Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons.
feature_details.Unarmored Defense: While unarmored and shieldless, base AC = 10 + Dexterity + Wisdom modifiers.

feature_details.Monk's Focus: Focus Points (count per the table) fuel three known features (expended points return on a Short or Long Rest; DC for saves = 8 + Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus): **Flurry of Blows** — expend 1 to make two Unarmed Strikes as a Bonus Action. **Patient Defense** — Bonus Action Disengage; expend 1 to also Dodge. **Step of the Wind** — Bonus Action Dash; expend 1 to also Disengage and double your jump distance this turn.
feature_details.Unarmored Movement: Speed +10 ft while unarmored and shieldless; grows per the table.
feature_details.Uncanny Metabolism: When you roll Initiative, regain all Focus Points and roll your Martial Arts die to regain that many + your Monk level in HP. Once per Long Rest.

feature_details.Deflect Attacks: Reaction on being hit by an attack dealing Bludgeoning/Piercing/Slashing damage — reduce that damage by 1d10 + Dexterity modifier + Monk level. If reduced to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect force at a creature within 5 ft (melee) or within 60 ft and not behind Total Cover (ranged) — Dexterity save or take damage equal to two Martial Arts die rolls + Dexterity modifier (same type as the original attack).
feature_details.Monk Subclass: Choose Warrior of Mercy, Warrior of Shadow, Warrior of the Elements, or Warrior of the Open Hand. Gain each subclass feature at your Monk level or lower.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.
feature_details.Slow Fall: Reaction when you fall — reduce fall damage by 5x your Monk level.

feature_details.Extra Attack: Attack twice instead of once when you take the Attack action.
feature_details.Stunning Strike: Once per turn on hitting with a Monk weapon or Unarmed Strike, expend 1 Focus Point — target makes a Constitution save; fail: Stunned until start of your next turn; success: Speed halved until then, and the next attack against it before then has Advantage.

feature_details.Empowered Strikes: Unarmed Strike damage can be Force damage or its normal type, your choice.

feature_details.Evasion: On a Dexterity save for half damage, take none on success and half on failure. Doesn't work while Incapacitated.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Acrobatic Movement: While unarmored and shieldless, move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling.

feature_details.Heightened Focus: Improves the three Monk's Focus features — **Flurry of Blows**: 3 Unarmed Strikes instead of 2. **Patient Defense**: gain Temp HP equal to two Martial Arts die rolls when used. **Step of the Wind**: bring a willing Large-or-smaller creature within 5 ft along with you (no Opportunity Attacks for its movement).
feature_details.Self-Restoration: At the end of each of your turns, remove Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned from yourself (choose one). Also, forgoing food/drink doesn't cause Exhaustion.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Deflect Energy: Deflect Attacks now works against any damage type, not just Bludgeoning/Piercing/Slashing.

feature_details.Disciplined Survivor: Proficiency in all saving throws. On a failed save, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it (must use the new roll).

feature_details.Perfect Focus: When you roll Initiative without using Uncanny Metabolism, regain Focus Points up to 4 if you have 3 or fewer.

feature_details.Ability Score Improvement: Gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat you qualify for.

feature_details.Superior Defense: At the start of your turn, expend 3 Focus Points for Resistance to all damage except Force, lasting 1 minute or until Incapacitated.

feature_details.Epic Boon: Gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat you qualify for; Boon of Irresistible Offense recommended.

feature_details.Body and Mind: Dexterity and Wisdom scores each increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

feature_details.Lay On Hands:
Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a Long Rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of Hit Points equal to five times your Paladin level.
  As a Bonus Action, you can touch a creature (which could be yourself) and draw power from the pool of healing to restore a number of Hit Points to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool.
  You can also expend 5 Hit Points from the pool of healing power to remove the Poisoned condition from the creature; those points don't also restore Hit Points to the creature.
feature_details.Spellcasting:
You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Paladin spells, which appear in the Paladin spell list later in the class's description.
  Spell Slots. The Paladin Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.
  Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Paladin spells. Heroism and Searing Smite are recommended.
  The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Paladin levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Paladin Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Paladin spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Paladin Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Paladin, your list of prepared spells can include six Paladin spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.
  If another Paladin feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Paladin spells for you.
  Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Paladin spell for which you have spell slots.
  Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Paladin spells.

feature_details.Weapon Mastery:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longswords and Javelins.
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of Halberds and Flails.

feature_details.Fighting Style:
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see "Feats" for feats). Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.
  Blessed Warrior. You learn two Cleric cantrips of your choice (see the Cleric class's section for a list of Cleric spells). Guidance and Sacred Flame are recommended. The chosen cantrips count as Paladin spells for you, and Charisma is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Paladin level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Cleric cantrip.
feature_details.Paladin's Smite: You always have the Divine Smite spell prepared. In addition, you can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

feature_details.Channel Divinity:
You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes, using it to fuel magical effects. You start with one such effect: Divine Sense, which is described below. Other Paladin features give additional Channel Divinity effect options. Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, you choose which effect from this class to create.
  You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You gain an additional use when you reach Paladin level 11.
  If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.
  Divine Sense. As a Bonus Action, you can open your awareness to detect Celestials, Fiends, and Undead. For the next 10 minutes or until you have the Incapacitated condition, you know the location of any creature of those types within 60 feet of yourself, and you know its creature type. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the Hallow spell.
feature_details.Paladin Subclass: Choose Oath of Devotion, Oath of Glory, Oath of the Ancients, or Oath of Vengeance. Gain each subclass feature at your Paladin level or lower. Each oath's tenets and the level-3 features are the culmination of a Paladin's training.

feature_details.Faithful Steed: You always have Find Steed prepared, and can cast it once without a spell slot (regained on a Long Rest).

feature_details.Aura of Protection: 10-ft Emanation (inactive while Incapacitated) — you and allies inside gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum +1). With multiple Paladins present, a creature benefits from only one such aura at a time (its choice).

feature_details.Aura of Courage: You and allies are immune to Frightened while in your Aura of Protection (entering while already Frightened suppresses the condition there).

feature_details.Favored Enemy:

feature_details.Spellcasting:
You have learned to channel the magical essence of nature to cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Ranger spells, which appear in the Ranger spell list later in the class's description.

Ranger spells. Cure Wounds and Ensnaring Strike are recommended.

feature_details.Cunning Strike: When dealing Sneak Attack damage, forgo some Sneak Attack dice (removed before rolling) to add an effect immediately after damage; save DC = 8 + Dexterity modifier + Proficiency Bonus. **Poison** (cost 1d6, requires a Poisoner's Kit on you): Constitution save or Poisoned 1 minute (repeats save at end of its turns). **Trip** (cost 1d6): Large-or-smaller target fails a Dexterity save or is Prone. **Withdraw** (cost 1d6): move up to half your Speed immediately after the attack without Opportunity Attacks.

feature_details.Innate Sorcery:
An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with simmering magic. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash that magic for 1 minute, during which you gain the following benefits: - The spell save DC of your Sorcerer spells increases by 1.
- You have Advantage on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast.
You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a Long Rest.
feature_details.Spellcasting:
Drawing from your innate magic, you can cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Sorcerer spells, which appear in the Sorcerer spell list later in the class’s description.
Cantrips. You know four Sorcerer cantrips of your choice. Light, Prestidigitation, Shocking Grasp, and Sorcerous Burst are recommended. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Sorcerer levels 4 and 10, you learn another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Sorcerer Features table.
Spell Slots. The Sorcerer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.
Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Sorcerer spells. Burning Hands and Detect Magic are recommended.
The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Sorcerer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Sorcerer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Sorcerer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Sorcerer Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you’re a level 3 Sorcerer, your list of prepared spells can include six Sorcerer spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.
If another Sorcerer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Sorcerer spells for you.
Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots.
Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.
Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Sorcerer spells.
feature_details.Careful Spell: When casting a spell forcing a save, a number of creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum one) auto-succeed and take no damage even on a normally-half-damage success.
feature_details.Distant Spell: Double a spell's range (5+ ft), or change Touch range to 30 ft.
feature_details.Empowered Spell: Reroll a number of damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum one); must use new rolls.
feature_details.Extended Spell: Double a spell's duration (1 minute or longer) up to a max of 24 hours; if it requires Concentration, gain Advantage on saves to maintain it.
feature_details.Seeking Spell: On a missed spell attack roll, reroll the d20 and must use the new roll.
feature_details.Subtle Spell: Cast without Verbal, Somatic, or Material components (except Material components that are consumed or have a specified cost).
feature_details.Transmuted Spell: Change a spell's damage type (from Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder) to another type on that list.
feature_details.Twinned Spell: For a spell that can be upcast to target an extra creature (like Charm Person), increase its effective level by 1 instead of spending a slot for that purpose.

feature_details.Font of Magic:
You can tap into the wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by Sorcery Points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.
You have 2 Sorcery Points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer Features table. You can’t have more Sorcery Points than the number shown in the table for your level. You regain all expended Sorcery Points when you finish a Long Rest.
You can use your Sorcery Points to fuel the options below, along with other features, such as Metamagic, that use those points.
Converting Spell Slots to Sorcery Points. You can expend a spell slot to gain a number of Sorcery Points equal to the slot’s level (no action required).
Creating Spell Slots. As a Bonus Action, you can transform unexpended Sorcery Points into one spell slot. The Creating Spell Slots table shows the cost of creating a spell slot of a given level, and it lists the minimum Sorcerer level you must be to create a slot. You can create a spell slot no higher than level 5.
Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.

feature_details.Metamagic:
Because your magic flows from within, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from "Metamagic Options" later in this class’s description. You use the chosen options to temporarily modify spells you cast. To use an option, you must spend the number of Sorcery Points that it costs.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it unless otherwise noted in one of those options.
Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with one you don’t know. You gain two more options at Sorcerer level 10 and two more at Sorcerer level 17.
feature_details.Heightened Spell: One target of a save-forcing spell has Disadvantage on that save.
feature_details.Quickened Spell: Change an action-casting-time spell to a Bonus Action this casting; can't do this if you've already cast a level 1+ spell this turn, and can't cast another level 1+ spell this turn after.

feature_details.Sorcery Incarnate: If you have no Innate Sorcery uses left, you can still activate it by spending 2 Sorcery Points when you take the Bonus Action. While Innate Sorcery is active, you can use up to two Metamagic options per spell cast.

**Metamagic Options** (alphabetical; you know 2 starting at level 2, +2 more at level 10, +2 more at level 17; only one option per spell unless noted):

feature_details.Eldritch Invocations:
You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome. Invocations are described in the "Eldritch Invocation Options" section later in this class's description.
Prerequisites. If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Warlock level 5.
Replacing and Gaining Invocations. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.
When you gain certain Warlock levels, you gain more invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations column of the Warlock Features table.
You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.
feature_details.Pact Magic:
Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers.
The entity is a voice in the shadows—its identity unclear—but its boon to you is concrete: the ability to cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting.
The information below details how you use those rules with Warlock spells, which appear in the Warlock spell list later in the class's description.
Cantrips. You know two Warlock cantrips of your choice. Eldritch Blast and Prestidigitation are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Warlock cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Warlock levels 4 and 10, you learn another Warlock cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Warlock Features table.
Spell Slots. The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
For example, when you're a level 5 Warlock, you have two level 3 spell slots. To cast the level 1 spell Charm Person, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a level 3 spell.
Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells. Charm Person and Hex are recommended.
The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Warlock levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warlock Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Warlock spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level. When you reach level 6, for example, you learn a new Warlock spell, which can be of levels 1–3.
If another Warlock feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Warlock spells for you.
Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Warlock spell of an eligible level.
Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is the spellcasting ability for your Warlock spells.
Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Warlock spells.

feature_details.Magical Cunning: You can perform an esoteric rite for 1 minute. At the end of it, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots but no more than a number equal to half your maximum (round up). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

feature_details.Arcane Recovery:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover.
The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher.
For example, if you’re a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels’ worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.
Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
feature_details.Ritual Adept: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn’t have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.
feature_details.Spellcasting:
As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting.
The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the Wizard spell list later in the class’s description.
Cantrips. You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended.
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.
another Wizard cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Wizard Features table.
Spellbook. Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds, contains 100 pages, and can be read only by you or someone casting Identify. You determine the book’s appearance and materials, such as a gilt-edged tome or a collection of vellum bound with twine.
The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice.
Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table.
The spells are the culmination of arcane research you do regularly.
Spell Slots. The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.
Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose four spells from your spellbook. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you’re a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.
If another Wizard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Wizard spells for you.
Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.
Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.
Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

subclasses.name: Path of the Berserker
subclasses.subclass_flavor: Barbarians who walk the Path of the Berserker direct their Rage primarily toward violence. Their path is one of untrammeled fury, and they thrill in the chaos of battle as they allow their Rage to seize and empower them.
desc: Barbarians who walk the Path of the Berserker direct their Rage primarily toward violence. Their path is one of untrammeled fury, and they thrill in the chaos of battle as they allow their Rage to seize and empower them.

feature_details.Frenzy: If you use Reckless Attack while raging, deal extra damage to the first target hit on your turn with a Strength-based attack — roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus (same damage type as the weapon/Unarmed Strike).

feature_details.Mindless Rage: Immunity to Charmed and Frightened while raging; either condition ends on you when you enter Rage.

feature_details.Retaliation: When you take damage from a creature within 5 ft, you can use a Reaction to make one melee attack against it.

feature_details.Intimidating Presence: As a Bonus Action, each creature of your choice in a 30-ft Emanation must make a Wisdom save (DC 8 + Strength modifier + Proficiency Bonus); on a failure, Frightened 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns. Once per Long Rest, restorable by expending a use of Rage (no action required).

subclasses.name: Path of the Wild Heart
subclasses.subclass_flavor: Barbarians who follow the Path of the Wild Heart view themselves as kin to animals. These Barbarians learn magical means to communicate with animals, and their Rage heightens their connection to animals as it fills them with supernatural might.
desc: Barbarians who follow the Path of the Wild Heart view themselves as kin to animals. These Barbarians learn magical means to communicate with animals, and their Rage heightens their connection to animals as it fills them with supernatural might.

feature_details.Animal Speaker: Cast Beast Sense and Speak with Animals, but only as Rituals. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them.
feature_details.Rage of the Wilds: Whenever you activate your Rage, choose one: **Bear** — Resistance to every damage type except Force, Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant while raging; **Eagle** — when you activate Rage, take the Disengage and Dash actions as part of that Bonus Action, and while raging you can take a Bonus Action to take both actions again; **Wolf** — while raging, allies have Advantage on attack rolls against any enemy of yours within 5 ft of you.

feature_details.Aspect of the Wilds: Choose one (changeable on a Long Rest): **Owl** — Darkvision 60 ft, or +60 ft range if you already have it; **Panther** — Climb Speed equal to your Speed; **Salmon** — Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

feature_details.Nature Speaker: Cast Commune with Nature, but only as a Ritual. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

feature_details.Power of the Wilds: Whenever you activate your Rage, choose one: **Falcon** — Fly Speed equal to your Speed while raging if unarmored; **Lion** — while raging, enemies within 5 ft of you have Disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you or another Barbarian with this option active; **Ram** — while raging, a melee hit against a Large-or-smaller creature can give it the Prone condition.

subclasses.name: Path of the World Tree
subclasses.subclass_flavor: Barbarians who follow the Path of the World Tree connect with the cosmic tree Yggdrasil through their Rage. This tree grows among the Outer Planes, connecting them to each other and the Material Plane. These Barbarians draw on the tree's magic for vitality and as a means of dimensional travel.
desc: Barbarians who follow the Path of the World Tree connect with the cosmic tree Yggdrasil through their Rage. This tree grows among the Outer Planes, connecting them to each other and the Material Plane. These Barbarians draw on the tree's magic for vitality and as a means of dimensional travel.

feature_details.Vitality of the Tree: **Vitality Surge** — when you activate Rage, gain Temp HP equal to your Barbarian level. **Life-Giving Force** — at the start of each turn while raging, choose another creature within 10 ft to gain Temp HP equal to a number of d6s (equal to your Rage Damage bonus) added together; unused Temp HP vanishes when Rage ends.

feature_details.Branches of the Tree: Whenever a creature you can see starts its turn within 30 ft of you while raging, you can take a Reaction to summon spectral branches around it — Strength save (DC 8 + Strength modifier + Proficiency Bonus) or be teleported to an unoccupied space within 5 ft of you (or nearest unoccupied space); you can then reduce its Speed to 0 until end of the current turn.

feature_details.Battering Boots: During your turn, your reach is 10 ft greater with any Melee weapon with the Heavy or Versatile property; on a hit with such a weapon on your turn, you can activate the Push or Topple mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you're using.

feature_details.Travel along the Tree: When you activate Rage, and as a Bonus Action while raging, teleport up to 60 ft to an unoccupied space you can see. Once per Rage, extend the range to 150 ft and bring up to six willing creatures within 10 ft of you, each teleporting to an unoccupied space of your choice within 10 ft of your destination.

subclasses.name: College of Lore
subclasses.subclass_flavor: Bards of the College of Lore collect spells and secrets from diverse sources, such as scholarly tomes, mystical rites, and peasant tales. The college's members gather in libraries and universities to share their lore with one another. They also meet at festivals or affairs of state, where they can expose corruption, unravel lies, and poke fun at self-important figures of authority.
desc: Bards of the College of Lore collect spells and secrets from diverse sources, such as scholarly tomes, mystical rites, and peasant tales. The college's members gather in libraries and universities to share their lore with one another. They also meet at festivals or affairs of state, where they can expose corruption, unravel lies, and poke fun at self-important figures of authority.

feature_details.Bonus Proficiencies: You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
feature_details.Cutting Words: When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of yourself makes a damage roll or succeeds on an ability check or attack roll, you can take a Reaction to expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration; roll your Bardic Inspiration die, and subtract the number rolled from the creature's roll, reducing the damage or potentially turning the success into a failure.

feature_details.Magical Discoveries: You learn two spells of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list (or any combination). A spell you choose must be a cantrip or a spell for which you have spell slots. You always have the chosen spells prepared, and whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of the spells with another that meets these requirements.

feature_details.Peerless Skill: When you make an ability check or attack roll and fail, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration; roll the Bardic Inspiration die, and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning a failure into a success. On a failure, the Bardic Inspiration isn't expended.

feature_details.Dazzling Footwork: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield: Dance Virtuoso (Advantage on Charisma (Performance) checks involving dancing); Unarmored Defense (base AC = 10 + Dexterity + Charisma modifiers); Agile Strikes (when you expend a use of Bardic Inspiration as part of an action/Bonus Action/Reaction, you can make one Unarmed Strike as part of it); Bardic Damage (use Dexterity for Unarmed Strike attack rolls, and can deal Bludgeoning damage equal to a Bardic Inspiration die roll + Dexterity modifier instead of normal damage, without expending the die).

feature_details.Inspiring Movement: When an enemy you can see ends its turn within 5 feet of you, you can take a Reaction and expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to move up to half your Speed; one ally within 30 feet can also move up to half their Speed as a Reaction. None of this movement provokes Opportunity Attacks.
feature_details.Tandem Footwork: When you roll Initiative (and lack the Incapacitated condition), you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration; roll the die, and you and each ally within 30 feet who can see or hear you gain a bonus to Initiative equal to the number rolled.

feature_details.Leading Evasion: When subjected to an effect allowing a Dexterity save for half damage, you take no damage on a success and half on a failure instead. Creatures within 5 feet of you making the same save can share this benefit. Doesn't work if you're Incapacitated.

feature_details.Beguiling Magic: You always have Charm Person and Mirror Image prepared. Immediately after casting an Enchantment or Illusion spell with a spell slot, you can force a creature within 60 feet to make a WIS save vs your spell save DC. Fail: Charmed or Frightened (your choice) 1 min, repeats save at end of turns. Once per Long Rest, restorable by expending a Bardic Inspiration use.
feature_details.Mantle of Inspiration: As a Bonus Action, expend a Bardic Inspiration use and roll the die; choose creatures within 60 ft up to your CHA modifier (min. 1); each gains Temp HP equal to 2x the roll, then can use a Reaction to move up to their Speed without Opportunity Attacks.

feature_details.Mantle of Majesty: You always have Command prepared. As a Bonus Action, cast it without a spell slot, taking on an unearthly appearance for 1 min or until Concentration ends; during this time you can cast Command again as a Bonus Action without a slot, and Charmed creatures auto-fail their save. Once per Long Rest, restorable with a level 3+ slot.

feature_details.Unbreakable Majesty: As a Bonus Action, assume a majestic presence for 1 min or until Incapacitated; whenever a creature hits you with an attack roll for the first time on a turn, it must succeed a CHA save vs your spell save DC or the attack misses instead. Once per Short/Long Rest.

feature_details.Combat Inspiration: A creature holding a Bardic Inspiration die from you can use it for: Defense (Reaction when hit by an attack, add the roll to AC against that attack, possibly causing a miss) or Offense (immediately after hitting with an attack, add the roll to the damage).
feature_details.Martial Training: Gain proficiency with Martial Weapons and training with Medium Armor and Shields; can use a Simple or Martial weapon as a Spellcasting Focus for Bard spells.

feature_details.Extra Attack: Attack twice instead of once when you take the Attack action; can cast a cantrip with a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.

feature_details.Battle Magic: After casting a spell with a casting time of an action, make one weapon attack as a Bonus Action.

subclasses.name: Life Domain
subclasses.subclass_flavor: The Life Domain focuses on the positive energy that helps sustain all life in the multiverse. Clerics who tap into this domain are masters of healing, using that life force to cure many hurts. Existence itself relies on the positive energy associated with this domain, so a Cleric of almost any religious tradition might choose it. This domain is particularly associated with agricultural deities, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community. Religious orders of healing also seek the magic of this domain.

Existence itself relies on the positive energy associated with this domain, so a Cleric of almost any religious tradition might choose it. This domain is particularly associated with agricultural deities, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community. Religious orders of healing also seek the magic of this domain.

feature_details.Life Domain Spells: Always prepared — Aid, Bless, Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration (L3); Mass Healing Word, Revivify (L5); Aura of Life, Death Ward (L7); Greater Restoration, Mass Cure Wounds (L9).
feature_details.Disciple of Life: When a spell you cast with a spell slot restores HP to a creature, that creature regains additional HP equal to 2 plus the spell slot's level.
feature_details.Preserve Life: As a Magic action, present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of Channel Divinity to evoke healing energy equal to 5x your Cleric level; choose Bloodied creatures within 30 ft (can include you) and divide the HP among them. Can't restore a creature above half its HP maximum.

feature_details.Life Domain Spells: Always prepared — Aid, Bless, Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration (L3); Mass Healing Word, Revivify (L5); Aura of Life, Death Ward (L7); Greater Restoration, Mass Cure Wounds (L9).
Always prepared — Aid, Bless, Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration (L3); Mass Healing Word, Revivify (L5); Aura of Life, Death Ward (L7); Greater Restoration, Mass Cure Wounds (L9).
Always prepared — Aid, Bless, Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration (L3); Mass Healing Word, Revivify (L5); Aura of Life, Death Ward (L7); Greater Restoration, Mass Cure Wounds (L9).

feature_details.Blessed Healer: Immediately after casting a spell with a spell slot that restores HP to a creature other than yourself, you regain HP equal to 2 plus the spell slot's level.

feature_details.Supreme Healing: When you would roll dice to restore HP with a spell or Channel Divinity, don't roll — use the highest possible number for each die instead.

subclasses.name: Light Domain
subclasses.subclass_flavor: The Light Domain emphasizes the divine power to bring about blazing fire and revelation. Clerics who wield this power are enlightened souls infused with radiance and the power of their deities' discerning vision, charged with chasing away lies and burning away darkness.
desc: The Light Domain emphasizes the divine power to bring about blazing fire and revelation. Clerics who wield this power are enlightened souls infused with radiance and the power of their deities' discerning vision, charged with chasing away lies and burning away darkness.

feature_details.Light Domain Spells: Always prepared — Burning Hands, Faerie Fire, Scorching Ray, See Invisibility (L3); Daylight, Fireball (L5); Arcane Eye, Wall of Fire (L7); Flame Strike, Scrying (L9).
feature_details.Radiance of the Dawn: As a Magic action, present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of Channel Divinity to emit a flash of light in a 30-ft Emanation; dispels any magical darkness there. Each creature you choose there makes a Constitution save — fail: 2d10 + Cleric level Radiant damage; success: half.
feature_details.Warding Flare: When a creature you can see within 30 ft makes an attack roll, use a Reaction to impose Disadvantage on it. Uses equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), regained on a Long Rest.

feature_details.Light Domain Spells: Always prepared — Burning Hands, Faerie Fire, Scorching Ray, See Invisibility (L3); Daylight, Fireball (L5); Arcane Eye, Wall of Fire (L7); Flame Strike, Scrying (L9).
Always prepared — Burning Hands, Faerie Fire, Scorching Ray, See Invisibility (L3); Daylight, Fireball (L5); Arcane Eye, Wall of Fire (L7); Flame Strike, Scrying (L9).
Always prepared — Burning Hands, Faerie Fire, Scorching Ray, See Invisibility (L3); Daylight, Fireball (L5); Arcane Eye, Wall of Fire (L7); Flame Strike, Scrying (L9).

feature_details.Improved Warding Flare: Warding Flare uses regain on a Short or Long Rest instead of only Long Rest; whenever you use it, you can also give the triggering attack's target Temp HP equal to 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier.

feature_details.Corona of Light: As a Magic action, emit an aura of sunlight for 1 minute (or until dismissed, no action required) — Bright Light in a 60-ft radius, Dim Light 30 ft further. Enemies in the Bright Light have Disadvantage on saves against your Radiance of the Dawn and any spell dealing Fire or Radiant damage. Uses equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), regained on a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Trickery Domain
subclasses.subclass_flavor: The Trickery Domain offers magic of deception, illusion, and stealth. Clerics who wield this magic are a disruptive force in the world, puncturing pride, mocking tyrants, freeing captives, and flouting hollow traditions. They prefer subterfuge and pranks to direct confrontation.
desc: The Trickery Domain offers magic of deception, illusion, and stealth. Clerics who wield this magic are a disruptive force in the world, puncturing pride, mocking tyrants, freeing captives, and flouting hollow traditions. They prefer subterfuge and pranks to direct confrontation.

feature_details.Trickery Domain Spells: Always prepared — Charm Person, Disguise Self, Invisibility, Pass without Trace (L3); Hypnotic Pattern, Nondetection (L5); Confusion, Dimension Door (L7); Dominate Person, Modify Memory (L9).
feature_details.Blessing of the Trickster: As a Magic action, grant yourself or a willing creature within 30 ft Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks; lasts until you finish a Long Rest or use this feature again.
feature_details.Invoke Duplicity: As a Bonus Action, expend a use of Channel Divinity to create a perfect visual illusion of yourself (intangible, doesn't occupy its space) in an unoccupied space within 30 ft; lasts 1 minute, ends early if dismissed (no action) or you're Incapacitated. While it persists: **Cast Spells** — cast as though you were in the illusion's space (using your own senses); **Distract** — when you and the illusion are both within 5 ft of a creature that can see it, you have Advantage on attack rolls against that creature; **Move** — as a Bonus Action, move the illusion up to 30 ft to an unoccupied space within 120 ft of you.

feature_details.Trickery Domain Spells: Always prepared — Charm Person, Disguise Self, Invisibility, Pass without Trace (L3); Hypnotic Pattern, Nondetection (L5); Confusion, Dimension Door (L7); Dominate Person, Modify Memory (L9).
Always prepared — Charm Person, Disguise Self, Invisibility, Pass without Trace (L3); Hypnotic Pattern, Nondetection (L5); Confusion, Dimension Door (L7); Dominate Person, Modify Memory (L9).
Always prepared — Charm Person, Disguise Self, Invisibility, Pass without Trace (L3); Hypnotic Pattern, Nondetection (L5); Confusion, Dimension Door (L7); Dominate Person, Modify Memory (L9).

feature_details.Trickster's Transposition: Whenever you take the Bonus Action to create or move the Invoke Duplicity illusion, you can instead teleport to swap places with it.

feature_details.Improved Duplicity: **Shared Distraction** — you and allies attacking a creature within 5 ft of the illusion have Advantage; **Healing Illusion** — when the illusion ends, you or a creature of your choice within 5 ft of it regains HP equal to your Cleric level.

subclasses.name: War Domain
subclasses.subclass_flavor: War has many manifestations. It can make heroes of ordinary people. It can be desperate and horrific, with acts of cruelty and cowardice eclipsing instances of excellence and courage. Clerics who tap into the magic of the War Domain excel in battle, inspiring others to fight the good fight or offering acts of violence as prayers.
desc: War has many manifestations. It can make heroes of ordinary people. It can be desperate and horrific, with acts of cruelty and cowardice eclipsing instances of excellence and courage. Clerics who tap into the magic of the War Domain excel in battle, inspiring others to fight the good fight or offering acts of violence as prayers.

feature_details.War Domain Spells: Always prepared — Guiding Bolt, Magic Weapon, Shield of Faith, Spiritual Weapon (L3); Crusader's Mantle, Spirit Guardians (L5); Fire Shield, Freedom of Movement (L7); Hold Monster, Steel Wind Strike (L9).
feature_details.Guided Strike: When you or a creature within 30 ft misses with an attack roll, expend a use of Channel Divinity to give that roll a +10 bonus (Reaction required if benefiting another creature).
feature_details.War Priest: As a Bonus Action, make one attack with a weapon or Unarmed Strike. Uses equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), regained on a Short or Long Rest.

feature_details.War Domain Spells: Always prepared — Guiding Bolt, Magic Weapon, Shield of Faith, Spiritual Weapon (L3); Crusader's Mantle, Spirit Guardians (L5); Fire Shield, Freedom of Movement (L7); Hold Monster, Steel Wind Strike (L9).

feature_details.War God's Blessing: Expend a use of Channel Divinity to cast Shield of Faith or Spiritual Weapon without a spell slot; cast this way, the spell doesn't need Concentration — instead it lasts 1 minute, ending early if you recast it, become Incapacitated, or die.

feature_details.Avatar of Battle: You gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage (unconditional — no magic-weapon exception stated in the source text).

subclasses.name: Circle of the Land
subclasses.subclass_flavor: The Circle of the Land comprises mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites. These Druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of their communities.
desc: The Circle of the Land comprises mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites. These Druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of their communities.

feature_details.Circle of the Land Spells: Whenever you finish a Long Rest, choose one type of land — arid, polar, temperate, or tropical — and always have that land's spells prepared: Arid (Blur, Burning Hands, Fire Bolt at L3; Fireball at L5; Blight at L7; Wall of Stone at L9); Polar (Fog Cloud, Hold Person, Ray of Frost at L3; Sleet Storm at L5; Ice Storm at L7; Cone of Cold at L9); Temperate (Misty Step, Shocking Grasp, Sleep at L3; Lightning Bolt at L5; Freedom of Movement at L7; Tree Stride at L9); Tropical (Acid Splash, Ray of Sickness, Web at L3; Stinking Cloud at L5; Polymorph at L7; Insect Plague at L9).
feature_details.Land's Aid: As a Magic action, expend a Wild Shape use and choose a point within 60 ft; a 10-ft-radius Sphere of vitality-giving flowers and life-draining thorns appears there. Each creature you choose in the Sphere makes a CON save vs your spell save DC — fail: 2d6 Necrotic; success: half. One creature you choose in the area regains 2d6 HP. Both numbers increase by 1d6 at Druid levels 10 (3d6) and 14 (4d6).

feature_details.Natural Recovery: Cast one prepared Circle Spell (level 1+) without expending a slot, once per Long Rest. Also, on a Short Rest, recover spell slots with a combined level up to half your Druid level (round up, none level 6+) — once per Long Rest.

feature_details.Nature's Ward: Immune to the Poisoned condition; Resistance to a damage type tied to your current land choice — Arid: Fire; Polar: Cold; Temperate: Lightning; Tropical: Poison.

feature_details.Nature's Sanctuary: As a Magic action, expend a Wild Shape use to create a 15-ft Cube of spectral trees/vines on the ground within 120 ft, lasting 1 minute or until you're Incapacitated or die; you and allies there have Half Cover, and allies also gain your current Nature's Ward Resistance. As a Bonus Action, move the Cube up to 60 ft to ground within 120 ft of you.

feature_details.Circle Forms: Channels lunar magic into your Wild Shape forms. Your maximum CR equals your Druid level ÷ 3 (rounded down). Armor Class: while in the form, your AC equals 13 + your Wisdom modifier if that total is higher than the Beast's AC. Temporary Hit Points: you gain Temp HP equal to 3x your Druid level.
feature_details.Circle of the Moon Spells: You always have prepared — Cure Wounds, Moonbeam, Starry Wisp (level 3); Conjure Animals (level 5); Fount of Moonlight (level 7); Mass Cure Wounds (level 9). You can cast these while in Wild Shape form.

feature_details.Improved Circle Forms: While in Wild Shape — Lunar Radiance: each attack in Wild Shape can deal its normal damage type or Radiant damage (choose each time you hit). Increased Toughness: add your Wisdom modifier to Constitution saving throws.

feature_details.Moonlight Step: As a Bonus Action, teleport up to 30 ft to an unoccupied space you can see, with Advantage on your next attack roll before end of turn. Uses equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), regained on a Long Rest; also regainable by expending a level 2+ spell slot.

feature_details.Lunar Form: Improved Lunar Radiance — once per turn, deal an extra 2d10 Radiant damage on a hit with a Wild Shape attack. Shared Moonlight — whenever you use Moonlight Step, also teleport one willing creature within 10 ft of you to an unoccupied space within 10 ft of your destination.

feature_details.Circle of the Sea Spells: You always have prepared — Fog Cloud, Gust of Wind, Ray of Frost, Thunderwave (level 3); Lightning Bolt, Water Breathing (level 5); Control Water, Ice Storm (level 7); Conjure Elemental, Hold Monster (level 9).
feature_details.Wrath of the Sea: As a Bonus Action, expend a Wild Shape use to create a 5-ft Emanation lasting 10 minutes. When manifested and on subsequent turns as a Bonus Action, choose a creature in the Emanation — CON save vs your spell save DC or take Cold damage (d6s equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum one) and be pushed up to 15 ft away if Large or smaller.

feature_details.Aquatic Affinity: The Wrath of the Sea Emanation increases to 10 ft; you also gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

feature_details.Stormborn: Your Wrath of the Sea confers two more benefits while active — Flight (Fly Speed equal to your Speed) and Resistance (to Cold, Lightning, and Thunder damage).

feature_details.Oceanic Gift: Manifest Wrath of the Sea's Emanation around a willing creature within 60 ft instead of yourself; that creature gains all benefits, using your spell save DC and Wisdom modifier. You can manifest it around both yourself and another creature by expending two Wild Shape uses instead of one.

subclasses.name: Battle Master
subclasses.subclass_flavor: Battle Masters are students of the art of battle, learning martial techniques passed down through generations. The most accomplished Battle Masters are well-rounded figures who combine their carefully honed combat skills with academic study in the fields of history, theory, and the arts.
desc: Battle Masters are students of the art of battle, learning martial techniques passed down through generations. The most accomplished Battle Masters are well-rounded figures who combine their carefully honed combat skills with academic study in the fields of history, theory, and the arts.

feature_details.Combat Superiority: Learn 3 maneuvers of your choice (see Maneuver Options below); learn 2 more at levels 7, 10, and 15 (and can swap one known maneuver each time). You have 4 Superiority Dice (d8s, regained on a Short or Long Rest); +1 die at level 7 (5 total) and level 15 (6 total). Maneuver save DC = 8 + Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice) + Proficiency Bonus.
feature_details.Student of War: Gain proficiency with one type of Artisan's Tools and one skill from the level-1 Fighter skill list.

feature_details.Know Your Enemy: As a Bonus Action, learn whether a creature within 30 ft has any Immunities/Resistances/Vulnerabilities, and what they are. Once per Long Rest; restorable by expending a Superiority Die (no action required).

feature_details.Relentless: Once per turn when using a maneuver, roll 1d8 and use that instead of expending a Superiority Die.

feature_details.Ultimate Combat Superiority:
Superiority Die becomes a d12.
  - **Maneuver Options** (alphabetical): **Ambush** — add a Superiority Die to a Dexterity (Stealth) check or Initiative roll. **Bait and Switch** — swap places with a willing creature within 5 ft (5 ft movement, no Opportunity Attacks); roll the die, you or the creature gets that bonus to AC until your next turn. **Commander's Strike** — replace one attack to let a willing creature use its Reaction to attack, adding the die to its damage on a hit. **Commanding Presence** — add the die to a Charisma (Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion) check. **Disarming Attack** — on a hit, add the die to damage; target makes a Strength save or drops an item. **Distracting Strike** — on a hit, add the die to damage; the next attack against the target before your next turn has Advantage. **Evasive Footwork** — Bonus Action Disengage, add the die to your AC until your next turn. **Feinting Attack** — Bonus Action, Advantage on your next attack this turn against a target within 5 ft; if it hits, add the die to damage. **Goading Attack** — on a hit, add the die to damage; target fails a Wisdom save or has Disadvantage on attacks against others until end of your next turn. **Lunging Attack** — Bonus Action Dash; if you moved 5+ ft in a line before a melee hit this turn, add the die to damage. **Maneuvering Attack** — on a hit, add the die to damage; a willing creature can Reaction-move half its Speed without Opportunity Attacks from your target. **Menacing Attack** — on a hit, add the die to damage; target fails a Wisdom save or is Frightened until end of your next turn. **Parry** — Reaction on being damaged by a melee attack, reduce damage by the die roll + Strength or Dexterity modifier. **Precision Attack** — on a miss, roll the die and add to the attack roll, possibly turning it into a hit. **Pushing Attack** — on a hit, add the die to damage; Large-or-smaller target fails a Strength save or is pushed 15 ft away. **Rally** — Bonus Action, an ally within 30 ft gains Temp HP equal to the die roll + half your Fighter level (round down). **Riposte** — Reaction when a creature misses you with a melee attack, make a melee attack against it, adding the die to damage on a hit. **Sweeping Attack** — on a melee hit, a second creature within 5 ft of the target (and your reach) that the original roll would also hit takes damage equal to the die roll (same type). **Tactical Assessment** — add the die to an Intelligence (History or Investigation) or Wisdom (Insight) check. **Trip Attack** — on a hit, add the die to damage; Large-or-smaller target fails a Strength save or is Prone.

subclasses.name: Champion
subclasses.subclass_flavor: A Champion focuses on the development of martial prowess in a relentless pursuit of victory. Champions combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows, withstand peril, and garner glory. Whether in athletic contests or bloody battle, Champions strive for the crown of the victor.

Champions combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows, withstand peril, and garner glory. feature_details.Improved Critical: Weapon and Unarmed Strike attacks score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20.
feature_details.Remarkable Athlete: Advantage on Initiative rolls and Strength (Athletics) checks. Immediately after scoring a Critical Hit, move up to half your Speed without Opportunity Attacks.

feature_details.Additional Fighting Style: Gain another Fighting Style feat of your choice.

feature_details.Heroic Warrior: During combat, give yourself Heroic Inspiration whenever you start your turn without it.

feature_details.Survivor: **Defy Death** — Advantage on Death Saving Throws; rolling 18-20 counts as rolling a 20. **Heroic Rally** — at the start of each turn, regain 5 + Constitution modifier HP if Bloodied and at 1+ HP.

subclasses.subclass_flavor: Eldritch Knights combine the martial mastery common to all Fighters with a careful study of magic. Their spells both complement and extend their combat skills, providing additional protection to shore up their armor and also allowing them to engage many foes at once with explosive magic.

feature_details.Arcane Charge: When you use Action Surge, teleport up to 30 ft to an unoccupied space you can see (before or after the additional action).

feature_details.Improved War Magic: When you take the Attack action, replace two attacks with a casting of a level 1 or 2 Wizard spell with a casting time of an action.
